capsule.eyebrow: GI tract screening · no tube, no sedation
capsule.title: Anhan AI magnetically guided capsule endoscopy
capsule.summary: A capsule a touch bigger than a leading fish-oil tablet records the stomach and bowel as it moves naturally, then leaves the body on its own. No sedation, no tube.

ai_led.title: AI-assisted reading
ai_led.body: Magnetic positioning and an imaging AI model flag suspicious frames for physician review.

no_tube.title: No tube, no sedation
no_tube.body: You swallow the capsule with a sip of water. There is no traditional endoscope and no anesthesia.

single_use.title: Single-use
single_use.body: The capsule is a single-use medical device. It exits naturally and is not recovered or reused.

who.title: Who it is for
who.body: Adults with upper abdominal discomfort, chronic gastritis follow-up, a family history of gastric cancer, or anyone avoiding conventional endoscopy. Pregnant patients and people with implanted pacemakers should consult their physician first.

preparation.title: How to prepare
bullets: Eat only clear or semi-liquid food the day before and fast for 8 to 10 hours
Stop iron and bismuth-containing medicines 3 days ahead
People with diabetes should adjust medication with their physician in advance

process.title: What happens during the procedure
steps: Sign the consent form and put on the data recorder belt
Swallow the capsule with a small sip of water
Magnetic guidance captures images of the stomach and bowel
Physician reads the images with AI support, report in 3 to 5 business days
The capsule exits naturally; no recovery needed

risk.title: Risks and cautions
risk.body: Capsule retention is rare but possible. People with known bowel obstruction or severe strictures should not have this test. Avoid strong magnetic fields on the day of the test.

cardiac.eyebrow: Coronary screening · no radiation, no contrast
cardiac.title: Cardiac MR angiography (MRCA)
cardiac.summary: A 3.0T MRI scanner images the coronary arteries without iodinated contrast and without ionizing radiation, suitable for repeat follow-up.

no_radiation.title: No ionizing radiation
no_radiation.body: Magnetic imaging replaces X-rays, so it can be used for routine follow-up.

no_contrast.title: No contrast agent
no_contrast.body: No iodinated or gadolinium contrast is injected, which suits people with allergies or reduced kidney function.

breath_hold.title: 14-second breath hold
breath_hold.body: Each scan needs a 14-second breath hold. The full study takes 30 to 45 minutes.

who.title: Who it is for
who.body: Adults with chest tightness, chest pain, or a family history of coronary disease; people allergic to CT contrast who wish to reduce radiation exposure; anyone with an abnormal screening ECG needing further evaluation.

preparation.title: How to prepare
bullets: Skip caffeine on the day of the test
Practice a 14-second breath hold and follow the technician's rhythm
Pacemakers, implantable defibrillators, and aneurysm clips are contraindications; disclose implants in advance

process.title: What happens during the procedure
steps: Sign the consent form and remove metal accessories
Practice the breath-hold rhythm and connect the ECG gating leads
Multiple angle scans inside the bore
Physician reads and post-processes the images, report in 2 to 3 business days
Physician reviews the report with you in person or by video

risk.title: Risks and cautions
risk.body: MRI itself produces no ionizing radiation, but implanted metal can be affected by the magnetic field. Disclose all prior surgeries and implants before the scan.
